title: plotyy
summary: Plot two data sets with independent left and right Y axes.
description: `plotyy` creates two overlaid Cartesian axes in the current figure, plots the first data set against the left Y axis, plots the second data set against the right Y axis, and returns the axes and line handles. It is a legacy MATLAB compatibility helper; new MATLAB code generally uses `yyaxis`.
syntax: [ax, h1, h2] = plotyy(X1, Y1, X2, Y2)
[ax, h1, h2] = plotyy(X1, Y1, X2, Y2, fun)
[ax, h1, h2] = plotyy(X1, Y1, X2, Y2, fun1, fun2)

arguments.name: X1, Y1
arguments.description: Data plotted against the left Y axis. Data shape handling is delegated to the low-level `line` primitive.

arguments.name: X2, Y2
arguments.description: Data plotted against the right Y axis. Data shape handling is delegated to the low-level `line` primitive.

arguments.name: fun, fun1, fun2
arguments.description: Optional plotting function selectors. Supported values are `plot`, `line`, `semilogx`, `semilogy`, and `loglog`.

outputs.name: h1
outputs.description: Line handle or handles for the left axes.

outputs.name: h2
outputs.description: Line handle or handles for the right axes.

examples.description: Plot two series with separate Y axes

notes: `plotyy` returns the left axes as the current axes after plotting.
The right axes shares the primary plot viewport and stores `YAxisLocation` as `right`.
For compatibility with existing RunMat plotting primitives, line creation uses the same handle and data-shape behavior as `line`.
gpu_residency: `plotyy` is a plotting sink. It delegates line creation to the existing low-level `line` path, so GPU-resident inputs follow the same residency behavior as `line` and are not gathered by `plotyy` itself.
